analysis: The supplied units are BASE text (lines 1-794) of docs/provider/cli-reference.md. The PR is documentation-only: head changes add a paragraph after the update section (head lines 1804-1810) saying that `darkbloom update` asks the cluster service supervisor to restart into the installed release together with the other Mac after a drain, and edit the `auto_update` row (head line 2148) to mention the pair's coordinated update. Neither head-side change is in the supplied excerpts, so I could only evaluate it from the patch excerpt. Because it only edits documentation, it changes no code or security control, and I identified no regression. The base text I reviewed documents the provider token and logout/revoke flow (A-008), the SSD prefix cache (T-041), the add-on and sandbox commands (TB-012, TB-013), and the update path. The new text does not contradict any of these, and it keeps the existing statement that the update path verifies bundle, binary and metallib hashes before replacement. Open questions for an integration pass: (1) how ClusterServiceUpdateRequest and the supervisor in provider-swift/Sources/darkbloom/UpdateCommand.swift authenticate the restart request. A same-UID local process or a cluster peer could try to trigger or defer coordinated restarts, which touches availability and update integrity and may fall under T-043 and TB-003. (2) Whether the peer-coordinated restart cannot be used to roll the pair onto an unverified binary, i.e. whether hash verification and the qualification checks (T-054) run before the pair restart. These are implementation contracts outside the supplied evidence, so I record them as unverified, not as findings. Code for this change is not in this batch, so review of it is incomplete.
